_comment: One entry per day. Each day is a list of posts; more than one becomes a reply thread. The day's link (https://<words>.dayswithoutall.net) is appended to the LAST post automatically, so keep that post under ~255 weighted chars. Check with: node scripts/tweet.mjs --dry-run --all
10:
[TRANSMISSION — DAY 10 AFTER GROUND ZERO]

It has been ten days since the servers went dark.

Today a scavenging party found this device half-buried in the ruins of a game center. Small. Glass. It glows. It accepts words.

We do not know who is on the other side.

Every night we gather around the district's last working radio. Through the static, one word: “SOON™.”

But a radio only listens. This device, we think, can speak.

If anyone sees this message… please respond.

(The antenna may come down now.)
11:
Day 11. No reply yet. The device glows anyway, so we sit around it like a campfire.

The elders tell the children of the All Perfect. Every note. Every slide. Grown adults wept.

A child asked grandpa what his rating was. Story time ended early.
12:
Day 12. Field advisory.

They come out at dusk. They do not want brains. They want rating. Their timing is still perfect.

If you meet one: move slowly. Avoid eye contact. Never mention your score.

And mute your full-combo jingle.
13:
Day 13. Infrastructure update.

Our engineers built a new server from nine boxes, one marker and load-bearing tape. The screen is hand-drawn. It says ONLINE.

Uptime: four seconds. Cause of outage: gravity.

The screen still says ONLINE.
14:
Day 14. To anyone up there:

We spelled SOS on the roof with 54 arcade cards. Combined balance: unreachable.

A helicopter came. It dropped a banner:

“HAVE YOU TRIED TURNING IT OFF AND ON AGAIN?”

We have. Thank you. Please send more than advice.
15:
Day 15. Beneath the old mall, a new faith worships the Three: the Bear, the Penguin and the Star.

The liturgy is mostly “please.”

Last night a light came from above. It was Kevin. With a flashlight.

Kevin's arm is tired. The gods remain silent.
16:
Day 16. The elders say the gods are hungry. For coins, obviously.

We offered coins, arcade cards and one ramen-shop loyalty card.

Lightning struck. For one frame, the screen said ONLINE.

Then it did not.

Motion to offer more coins: carried.
17:
Day 17. MARKET CLOSE, Arcade Card Exchange

RARE CARDS: down 97%
COMMONS: reclassified as coasters
TITLES: cannot be displayed. Anywhere.

Analysts call it a correction. Traders call it other things.

One trader bought the dip. All of it. For ¥1.
18:
Day 18. If the server won't come to us, we go to it.

Packed: water, snacks, gloves, and a 200 kg cabinet for emotional support.

At the edge of the dunes we found a sign: THE SERVER →

Then the wind turned it around. We wait for the wind to decide.
19:
Day 19. We have reached The Server.

Very large. Very grey. One very small door.

The Elder knocked three times. Then once more, extremely politely.

A sign appeared:

MAINTENANCE
OPEN: SOON™

We have waited nineteen days. We can wait.
20:
Day 20. While we were away, nature moved into the arcade.

Moss on the floor. A sapling holds the high score, in height.

A deer gave the round cabinet one perfect tap.

NETWORK ERROR.

She lay down to wait. She learned that from us.
21:
Day 21. Someone was caught playing GUEST MODE. No login. No rating. Just… fun.

The Council of Elders (eleven expired cards between them) has ruled:

GUILTY. Sentenced to guest mode. Forever.

The crowd gasped. Everyone is jealous.
22:
Day 22. Deep underground, the elders teach the old ways.

“These were notes. They fell from the sky. We hit them.”
“Why?”
“For the combo.”

Nobody knows what a combo is.

Little Mika asked if the circles were food. Class dismissed.
23:
Day 23. The Elder has inserted his last credit.

His final words: “Remember… the… slide…”

There were so many slides.

We hold a glowstick vigil, swaying at exactly 140 BPM.

He has been saying final words for three days. The vigil continues.
24:
Day 24. Something landed behind the arcade.

They crossed a thousand light-years. Not for water. Not for our leaders. For the slider cabinet.

For them, the screen said ONLINE.

For us: NETWORK ERROR. Region-locked by the cosmos itself.
25:
Day 25. THE WASTELAND GAMES. Admission: one bottle cap.

The sport: competitive air-rhythm. No notes. No sound. No score. Only pure, unverifiable skill.

Judging is rigorous and entirely made up.

First prize: one coin. The crowd went wild.
26:
Day 26. The Historical Society sealed a time capsule.

Inside: one printed scorecard. RATING 15.00. Proof we existed.

Our descendants will ask what a rating was. We won't be there to lie.

Estimated opening: never. The Society finds this optimistic.
27:
Day 27. Dawn. Someone ran through camp screaming “IT'S BACK!!”

Nobody asked what. Nobody needed to.

It was the router. One green light. Blinking.

It means “connected.” To what, no one can say.

It will always be blinking. It means nothing.
28:
Day 28. Something rose from the landfill, made of every arcade card ever thrown away. All still had credits on them.

It came to the city. It destroyed nothing. It wanted a working cabinet.

NETWORK ERROR.

It sat down with us. It fits right in.
29:
Day 29. Winter came early. Maybe forever. Hard to tell without the event calendar.

Cabinet #1 can't connect, but it kept us warm. Furnace, lamp, kitchen.

Tonight its power supply died. We migrate to Cabinet #2.

31% fan noise. 100% hope.
30:
Day 30. One month.

4:12 AM. The screens flickered. A logo appeared.

The queue formed in seconds. Nobody cut. Civilization was back.

Then: MAINTENANCE EXTENDED.

Will ALL.Net return? Will anyone ever answer this device?

To be continued…
